card.profile: Boogaloo or bugalú (also: shing-a-ling, Latin boogaloo, Latin R&B) is a modern jazz genre of Latin music and dance which was popular in the United States in the 1960s. Boogaloo originated in New York City mainly by stateside Cubans and Puerto Ricans with African American music influences. The style was a fusion of popular African American jazz, rhythm and blues (R&B) and soul music with mambo and son montuno, with songs in both English and Spanish. The American Bandstand television program introduced the dance and the music to the mainstream American audience.
card.insight: Though the dance craze only lasted until 1968/69, Latin boogaloo was popular enough that almost every major and minor Latin dance artist of the time recorded at least a few boogaloos on their albums.

steps.name: Basic double leg roll
steps.description: Put feet together, bend knees slightly, and roll both knees forward and to the sides on toes.

steps.name: Single leg rolls
steps.description: Feet shoulder-width apart, rolling one leg at a time while maintaining isolation.

steps.name: Hip Boogaloo Rolls
steps.description: Moving hips side to side while isolating upper body, then rolling in a circle.

steps.name: Boogaloo Chest
steps.description: Moving chest forward, right, back, left, and forward in a fluid motion.

steps.name: Head rolls
steps.description: Rolling the head while coordinating with body and chest movement.

steps.name: The Old Man
steps.description: Shifting lower body and upper body in alternating diagonal parts.
